title: LLM-as-a-Tutor: Policy-Aware Prompt Adaptation for Non-Verifiable RL
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Static training prompts often fail to challenge the policy; a tutor appends constraints and rubrics to restore discriminative signal.
layout: 2 regions, left-to-right; left prompt pools, right stacked prompt-rubric-response flow with mascots
description: The left side, titled "Static RL Training Corpora," has two grey ovals. The upper one holds non-challenging prompts, labeled in red, such as "write me birthday wish for nephew" and "What color is grass?". The lower one holds challenging prompts, labeled in green, such as a complex chord progression and a poem where every word starts with e. A dashed curve links one non-challenging prompt to the right side. The right side shows a vertical flow. An initial prompt and a single-item initial rubric sit above two similar grey policy responses that go to a llama labeled Policy LLM. A large down arrow leads to an adapted prompt and adapted rubrics. These add a 7-year-old who loves dinosaurs, with the added text underlined. They feed two differentiated responses, one dark (checked) and one light (crossed), to a second Policy LLM llama. A scarf-wearing Tutor LLM llama stands in the middle. Red marks the problem and green marks the fix.
caption: Overview of LLM-as-a-Tutor: when the policy's responses to a prompt are indistinguishable in quality, a tutor LLM adds a constraint to make the prompt more challenging. (Left) Static RL training corpora for non-verifiable tasks contain prompts that are non-challenging for the current policy and provide little learning signal. (Right) The tutor examines a pair of policy rollouts; if their quality is indistinguishable, the tutor appends a constraint and corresponding rubric criteria which turn the non-challenging prompt into a challenging one that elicits variance in rollouts.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for non-verifiable instruction following increasingly relies on LLM judges with prompt-specific rubrics as reward signals. While recent methods adapt these rubrics to the evolving policy during training, the training prompts themselves remain static, drawn from fixed corpora. This static approach often results in a critical misalignment between prompt difficulty and policy capability, leaving the judge unable to recover a discriminative reward signal when prompts fail to elicit quality variance among rollouts. To address this misalignment, we introduce LLM-as-a-Tutor, a framework that extends the LLM's role from judge to tutor: a single model serves as an examiner that pairwise-compares policy rollouts to detect non-challenging prompts, and as a generator that appends atomic constraints to them. This append-only design preserves the original prompt while adding constraints to increase difficulty in step with the policy's capability, producing a self-calibrating training signal without external difficulty schedules. On three complex instruction-following benchmarks, our method outperforms both policy-unaware baselines and prior policy-adaptive methods that adapt rubrics or rewrite prompts, on average and on four of five metrics, suggesting prompt adaptation as an underexplored axis of policy-awareness in non-verifiable RL for constraint-heavy instruction following.
